sparql:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX dtl: <http://www.DTL.org/schema/properties/>
PREFIX mo: <http://purl.org/ontology/mo/>
PREFIX foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/>
SELECT DISTINCT ?composer 
 WHERE {
 ?composer rdf:type mo:MusicArtist .
 ?composer foaf:name "%s" .
 ?tune rdf:type mo:MusicalWork .
 ?tune dtl:composed_by ?composer .
 }
gold_question: Is there more than one composer with this name in the graph?

model_output.nl_question: Who is the composer of a given tune (by name)?
model_output.confidence_rationale: No directly matching CQ item exists in the evidence. The SPARQL clearly finds composers (MusicArtist type) with a given name who composed tunes (MusicalWork via dtl:composed_by). However, confidence is reduced because this relies entirely on SPARQL interpretation without supporting NL evidence from the provided competency questions.

# ================================== START

PREFIX mtp: <http://w3id.org/polifonia/ontology/meetups-ontology#> 
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT DISTINCT ?resource ?placeLabel ?personIRI ?personLabel ?text
WHERE { 
 VALUES ?subject { <http://dbpedia.org/resource/Clara_Schumann> } 
 ?s mtp:hasSubject ?subject ; mtp:hasType ?type . 
 FILTER (regex ( str (?type), str ("HM") ) ) . 
 ?s mtp:hasPlace ?aPlaceIRI .

 OPTIONAL { ?resource rdfs:label ?placeLabel } .

 mtp:hasEvidenceText ?text .
 ?aParticipantIRI rdf:type mtp:Participant ;
 mtp:hasEntity ?personIRI .
 OPTIONAL { ?personIRI rdfs:label ?personLabel } . 
} ORDER BY ?s

sparql:
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX organs: <https://w3id.org/arco/ontology/organs/>
PREFIX core: <https://w3id.org/arco/ontology/core/>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?place
WHERE { 
?organ core:isDescribedBy ?project .
?project core:hasPlace ?place .
?place a core:PhysicalPlace . 
?project core:isFirstProject ?isFirstProject .
FILTER(xsd:Boolean(?isFirstProject) = True)
}
gold_question: For all organs in the graph, what are their original locations?

review.note:
It is taking the evidence too literally, the organ in the query is not constrained. 
It is an odd query, it's hard to understand why they use a boolean property to find the earliest date for an organ. Maybe the dates are of different form and cannot always be ordered. But there is no guarantee that there is only one FirstProject.

model_output.nl_question: Where is an organ located originally?
model_output.confidence_rationale: The evidence phrase directly captures the SPARQL semantics: selecting places from the first project description (isFirstProject=True), which represents the original location of an organ. The match is nearly verbatim with high relevance.
